entries.title: Each article has a guide in Chat
entries.body: Every article in your library has a guide, pinned at the top of Chat, that talks about how to read this piece: where to start, what to search for, which modes help, drawing on your profile and why you are reading. The first time you open an article in a wide enough window, it opens on the guide rather than Summary. When an answer suggests a passage, or a mode that opens without making anything new, it takes you there itself.

entries.title: Help answers your questions about Spideryarn
entries.body: Signed in, every Help page has an Ask about Spideryarn box: ask how something works or where you are stuck, and the answer appears as it is written, drawn from the Help pages and linking only to them. Help also has captioned screenshots throughout, and short moving demonstrations; if your device is set to reduce motion, you get stills. Your question is sent to the AI service with the Help pages but is not kept.

entries.title: Chat has a way back and message steps
entries.body: An open conversation has a labelled ‹ Chats button back to the list, instead of an unlabelled close icon. Buttons beneath it step between messages, in Learn and passage chats as well, and its information card names the AI that answered and how hard it was asked to think. Learn's Start over shows Starting over… at once, not a blank.

entries.title: Adding an article you already have costs nothing
entries.body: Pasting an article already in your library uses up no import; you are told so, with a button to open it. On someone else's public article, signed in, you are offered a private copy, or the copy you already have. An AI assistant you have connected to Spideryarn can ask for a private sharing link, which you approve each time.

entries.title: Buttons and text boxes match across modes
entries.body: Buttons and text boxes that do the same job look the same in every mode; step arrows in Diagram, Quotes and Skim are 44px or more. Failure messages share one warning colour, and rows of options that scroll fade at the edge when more lie beyond. Resting the pointer on a quote opens its card after 600ms, not 900ms.

entries.title: Referee can ask the AI about hidden text
entries.body: In Referee's Hidden text panel, a button asks the more capable AI to judge what the scan found, harmless typesetting or a planted instruction, only when you press it. Each finding is marked probably harmless or worth a look, with the reason beneath, or not checked. Referee is behind the Experimental features switch on your profile page.

entries.title: Pages fit after rotating an iPad or iPhone
entries.body: After turning an iPad or iPhone from landscape to portrait, the page could stay zoomed out, with the article short of the right edge and the bottom bar partway up the screen. It now fits the new width.

entries.title: Fixes to imports, Illustrated, Skim and Mirror
entries.body: Short blog posts could come in as their comment thread; they come in as the post. Illustrated could run out of time and publish a half-painted set; a slow picture now fails alone. Skim no longer errors before anything is made, Mirror offers a retry, not a blank, and a Stop pressed during the last step says what was kept.
